# AccessContextManagerServicePerimeter

`accesscontextmanager.gcp.hfl.dev/v1alpha1`

**Gap it fills.** Terraform's `google_access_context_manager_service_perimeter`. A VPC Service Controls perimeter of an access policy, with its enforced (status) and dry-run (spec) configurations; accessPolicy is the access policy's number. The ID starts with a letter, then letters, digits or _.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the accesscontextmanager.v1 Discovery document.

## Notes

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` (`docs/design.md`
section 2.4); its test is `pkg/discokind/kindtest` with the fixtures under
`pkg/controller/direct/accesscontextmanager/discokindtest/testdata/discokind/AccessContextManagerServicePerimeter/`.

A parallel kind for a resource Config Connector also manages (decision 19,
foundation item 21, 2026-11-23). Config Connector's Terraform-based
`AccessContextManagerServicePerimeter` lacks, in both the enforced
(`status`) and the dry-run (`spec`) configuration, an egress rule's
`sources` and `sourceRestriction`, ingress and egress rules' `roles` and
`title`, PSC endpoint sources (`pscEndpoint.forwardingRule`) and
`vpcAccessibleServices.allowedServicePatterns` and
`servicePatternsEnforcementScopes`; Terraform's update sends `status` or
`spec` whole, so no field kind beside it can own them. Ours owns the whole
perimeter: never beside Config Connector's perimeter or
`AccessContextManagerServicePerimeterResource` (which adds projects to a
perimeter's `status.resources`) for the same perimeter. To move one, make
ours with the same `resourceID` (it acquires the perimeter), then delete
Config Connector's object with `cnrm.cloud.google.com/deletion-policy:
abandon`.

`accessPolicy` is the access policy's number, and references are the
API's strings (`projects/<number>`, access level names). `perimeterType`
is immutable (Terraform forces a new perimeter for it); `etag` is left out.
Changes go through `servicePerimeters.patch` with a top-level mask, one
operation each; `commit` (moving the dry run to enforced) is not called:
change `status` instead.

Tested by kindtest on the fake (`pkg/discokind/fake`): create with
ingress and egress rules (sources, roles, titles, source restriction) and
an explicit dry-run spec, a resync, a changed rule and dry-run spec,
delete, abandon. The fake does not check the rules (which identities,
roles or services the API takes), the policy, or that a project is in one
regular perimeter only.

Live: pending, `live-skip`: an organization's access policy and Access
Context Manager roles on it, which the live-test account does not have.
With them, `task test-live PROJECT=$GCP_PROJECT KINDS=accesscontextmanager
LIVE_RUN=TestAccessContextManagerServicePerimeter`.
